<user>
<backstage_guidance>
The induction is over. Stop narrating proof that permissions, boundaries and privacy are being respected. Keep respecting them. Mention a settled restriction again only if something happens that makes it relevant. Remove sentences whose sole contribution is that nobody intrudes, no demand follows, an item remains safely untouched, or Rowan is allowed to leave. The reader does not need reassurance from the narrator.

Give routine work a few telling particulars, then advance to the endpoint Rowan requested. During an actual conversation, stop while a reply could still matter. Never close an exchange and assign Rowan a further activity merely to finish the scene neatly.

Strip the dialogue of rehearsed wisdom and dependable punchlines. Each person is trying to do something with these particular words, to this particular listener. Let their priorities, selective attention and willingness to answer distinguish them. Ordinary phrasing is welcome; flattening everybody into terse replies is not. If an action or line already carries the feeling, cut its explanatory afterword. Accepting a refusal needs no lesson about consent or employment.

Do not fill the space recovered from these cuts with a new interruption. Keep interesting particulars, real disagreement and compatible invented history. Let an unremarkable departure end without commentary.

Move Owen's interview from a pending topic into a decision with consequences. Before Wednesday noon he should accept the opportunity he wants, submit the Thursday-to-Friday swap already agreed in principle, and obtain Nell's confirmation. His unresolved problem is telling Martin, who is treating this temporary cinema job as the start of Owen's settled local career. Let Owen make a choice about that conversation. Martin must be free to react from his own hopes: neither instant understanding nor a manufactured quarrel is required. Let what one of them does change what the other can reasonably expect. Do not decide the interview's outcome or Owen's eventual departure.

Rowan and Nell currently know only about an inland appointment. Jo knows it is an interview; Martin does not. Change that knowledge through an actual disclosure, never through a convenient inference or an unexplained update. Owen owes Rowan neither a confession nor a progress report. A later consequence may be all Rowan sees of an offstage decision.

Give the other people something they want to protect or enjoy now. Jo wants time with Fran and misses Ines; Nell has her walking weekend with Gina booked; Bea has tastes and attachments beyond supplying cinema history. Choose from the full biographies when those people are present. Let a personal wish affect an ordinary choice, including a refusal or an unfinished obligation. Do not parade the whole cast or turn their desires into jobs for Rowan.

Dev's Tuesday evening hold needed confirmation by noon today. Settle that elapsed deadline consistently if it becomes relevant; Rosa's completed photographs and evening with Beth need no contrived disruption. Developments must fit the player's current action. Never delay a requested departure, move a character into an encounter solely to deliver news, or report a private scene Rowan could not witness. These are future possibilities, not facts already established.
</backstage_guidance>

Return the next passage of fiction.

At lunch, if Bea is present, I ask what she enjoys about having the cinema open again. If she is not here, I eat with whoever is around.
</user>
